title: Set 156

sentences.ko: 걔 좀 친해지면 진짜 웃긴데, 처음엔 좀 조용한 편이거든. 그러니까 처음에 좀 어색하더라도 한번 기회를 줘 봐, 알았지?
sentences.text: Okay, so he's really funny once he warms up, but he's kind of quiet at first, so if the beginning feels a little awkward, just give him a chance, alright?

alts.text: Heads up, he's kinda quiet at first, but he's hilarious once he loosens up, so if it's a little awkward early on, just give him a shot, okay?
He is genuinely very funny once he becomes comfortable, but he tends to be rather quiet at first, so if the beginning feels somewhat awkward, please give him a chance.

sentences.note: **warms up** 은 사람이 낯을 풀고 편해지는 것을 말해요. **give him a chance** 는 섣불리 판단하지 말고 한번 기회를 줘 보라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 요즘 자꾸 새벽 세 시쯤 깨는데, 그러면 머릿속으로 다음 날 할 일을 하나하나 다 훑기 시작해서, 다시 잠들 때쯤이면 알람이 곧 울릴 시간이야.
sentences.text: I keep waking up at like three in the morning, and then my brain starts going through everything I have to do the next day, so by the time I fall back asleep, my alarm's about to go off.

alts.text: Three in the morning, I'm wide awake again, and my brain starts running through my whole to-do list for tomorrow, so by the time I'm back asleep, my alarm's about to go off.

I have been repeatedly waking at around three in the morning, and my mind begins reviewing everything I need to do the following day, so by the time I fall asleep again, my alarm is just about to go off.

sentences.note: **I keep waking up** 처럼 keep 뒤에 ~ing 를 붙이면 자꾸 되풀이되는 일을 말해요. **about to go off** 는 알람이 막 울리려는 참이라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 우리 개는 천둥번개를 엄청 무서워해서, 비만 오면 침대 밑으로 비집고 들어가려고 해. 강아지 때 이후로는 거기에 몸이 들어가지도 않는데 말이야.
sentences.text: Our dog's terrified of thunderstorms, so every time it rains he tries to squeeze under the bed, even though he hasn't fit under there since he was a puppy.

alts.text: Thunderstorms totally freak our dog out, so whenever it rains he tries to cram himself under the bed, even though he hasn't fit under there since he was a puppy.
Our dog is terrified of thunderstorms, so whenever it rains he attempts to squeeze beneath the bed, even though he has not fit under it since he was a puppy.

sentences.note: **terrified of** 는 무언가를 몹시 무서워한다는 뜻이에요. **squeeze under** 는 좁은 틈 밑으로 몸을 비집고 들어가는 것을 말해요.

sentences.ko: 작동은 잘 되는데, 미리 솔직하게 말씀드리면 소리를 키우면 왼쪽 스피커가 살짝 지직거려요. 그래서 50달러만 받는 거예요.
sentences.text: It works fine, but I just want to be upfront that the left speaker crackles a little when you turn it up, and that's why I'm only asking fifty bucks for it.

alts.text: Just so you know, it works fine, but the left speaker crackles a bit when you crank it up, so that's why I'm only asking fifty bucks.
It functions properly, but I would like to be transparent that the left speaker crackles slightly at higher volumes, which is why I am asking only fifty dollars for it.

sentences.note: **be upfront** 는 숨기지 않고 미리 솔직하게 말한다는 뜻이에요. **crackles** 는 스피커가 지직거리는 소리를 내는 것이고, **bucks** 는 달러를 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 중고로 물건 팔면서 상태 솔직히 말하기

sentences.ko: 아니야 엄마, 밥 잘 먹고 있어, 진짜야. 요즘 요리할 시간이 별로 없어서 배달 음식을 많이 먹긴 했는데, 그래도 그것도 먹은 거잖아, 그치?
sentences.text: No, Mom, I'm eating fine, I promise. I just haven't had much time to cook lately, so it's been a lot of takeout, but that still counts as eating, right?

alts.text: I promise, Mom, I'm eating fine! I just haven't really had time to cook lately, so it's been a lot of takeout, but that still counts, right?
No, Mother, I am eating properly, I assure you. I simply have not had much time to cook recently, so I have been ordering a great deal of takeout, but surely that still counts as eating.

sentences.note: **takeout** 은 포장하거나 배달시켜 먹는 음식을 말해요. **that still counts as eating** 은 그래도 먹은 걸로 쳐 준다는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 부모님 안부 전화에서 잘 지낸다고 둘러대기

reviewed: 2번 formal 의 'my alarm is nearly due to sound' 는 원어민이 안 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이라 'my alarm is just about to go off' 로 고쳤습니다.
5번 formal 끝의 'does it not?' 은 소리내어 읽으면 옛날 말투처럼 들려서 'surely that still counts as eating.' 로 고쳤습니다.
